assumptions.value: 1 PIO state machine (a soft decoder) serves the board's one physical receiver input (V68 found: the board brings out 1 receiver input, not one per protocol); whichever of S.BUS/iBUS/SUMD/CRSF/SRXL2/JETI EX Bus is selected reuses that one SM, since no receiver PIO program is written and the tree does not fix a count (IOBoard.md:258, :281 'no receiver PIO program is written').
assumptions.why: R11's row and R4's row both leave the receiver decode method open ('P5 states the count it assumes ... and whether a bus uses a hardware UART instead'); with only 1 physical input (V68) and both hardware UARTs already booked (OpenYGE + VESC), a PIO program is the only free resource, and S.BUS is explicitly described in IOBoard.md:267 as 'received by a PIO program that is not written', which extends by analogy to the other framed buses on the same single input.
assumptions.source: checkout e13f5f60d2e5 hardware/docs/IOBoard.md:258, :267, :281; Research.md P5 row; FU-A3/008-P4-stock-R4.json placements figure for 'receiver inputs' (V68 found: 1 receiver input)

assumptions.value: 0 additional state machines beyond the 8 already booked for bidirectional DShot on the 4 multiprotocol ports: a port runs one protocol at a time, and the one-wire bootloader (19,200 baud), ESCape32 and Hitec D-series each fit inside the 2-SM/port allocation sized for bidirectional DShot, the heaviest mode a multiprotocol port can carry.
assumptions.why: IOBoard.md:258 states bidirectional DShot on the 4 multiprotocol ports already takes 8 of the 12 state machines, and no programmer protocol has run on a wire or has a written PIO program (IOBoard.md:261-265, 'no protocol has run on a wire'); since the ports are exclusive-mode, booking the DShot worst case as the ceiling avoids double-counting an SM that is never used concurrently with DShot on the same pin.
assumptions.source: checkout e13f5f60d2e5 hardware/docs/IOBoard.md:233-234, :258, :261-265; Research.md Agent layout, P5 row

budgets.value: Capacity 48 (RP2350B package, PICO_RP2350A=0; R1 confirms NUM_BANK0_GPIOS=48 applies to the IO board's own header). P5's own tally of committed signals: heartbeat in (1) + Link CAN controller SPI+INT+CS (5) + External CAN controller SPI+INT+CS (5, own bus assumed) + 20 output-port pins (20) + UART socket (2, half-duplex TX/RX both wired to the one line) + VESC's separate TX/RX lines (2, V67) + the one receiver input (1, V68) + 2 I2C buses (4) + encoder A/B/index after RS-422 translation (3) + load-cell ADC ADS1235 CS+DRDY (2, sharing an existing SPI bus) + thermocouple MAX31856 CS+fault (2, sharing a SPI bus) + phase-wire comparator output (1) + magnetic pickup output (1) + onboard/external pack-switch-driver enables (2) = 51, before the accelerometer path (0 to 4, Q4-dependent), the servo-converter/port-ceiling status lines (V115, V119, V135, not yet fixed) and the latch/clear read-back are added. This exceeds the 48-pin capacity on the currently selected part set even before those additions.

budgets.value: 32 words per block, 96 total. budgets.value: Capacity 2 hardware SPI blocks. Candidate users: Link CAN controller (MCP2518FDT-E/SL), External CAN controller (MCP2518FDT-E/SL), R13's load-cell ADC (ADS1235IRHBR), R12's motor-temperature thermocouple (MAX31856MUD+T), and, if Q4 picks the external-ADC alternative, R10's ADCS7476AIMFX/NOPB -- up to 5 SPI-protocol devices on 2 physical controllers. This is workable by multi-dropping several devices on one controller's SCK/MOSI/MISO with separate chip-selects and software-managed mode/clock switching between transactions (a standard pattern), but it has not been checked for timing conflict between the CAN controllers' continuous 10 MHz polling and the slower ADC/thermocouple transactions.

combinations.bind_order: The 4 multiprotocol ports bound first (in any relative order among themselves) with bidirectional DShot, then the one PPM-capable PWM port, then the receiver input.
combinations.outputs: 4 multiprotocol ports x bidirectional DShot (8 SM, 64 instruction words, 2 whole PIO blocks fully consumed at 2 ports/block) + 1 PPM output on one PWM port (1 SM, 4 words, 2 DMA channels, in the third block) + 1 receiver input (1 SM, word count not written, assumption above, remaining room in the third block) + the other 15 PWM-type ports on hardware PWM slices (no PIO cost).
combinations.resources: PIO: 10 of 12 state machines used (2 spare, both in the third block, PIO0 under a base-0 or base-16 assignment reaching whichever GPIO the receiver and any programmer function use), 68 of 96 instruction words used across the 3 blocks (32+32+4, third block has 28 words free). DMA: 2 of 16. PWM: 16 of 24 channels (12 slices) for the 16 PWM-type ports, provided the round-2 pin map avoids the stated 16-/8-apart collision spacing.
combinations.source: checkout e13f5f60d2e5 hardware/docs/IOBoard.md:107-109, :250, :258-259; pico-sdk 2.3.0 hardware_pio/pio.c:454-506, :66-81 as cited there; Research.md P5 row

combinations.bind_order: Any bind order that puts a fifth or sixth bidirectional-DShot-class device (for example, a programmer protocol implemented as its own 2-SM pair running concurrently with DShot on a different port, rather than reusing a port's own allocation) ahead of the receiver and PPM.
combinations.outputs: Would need an 11th or 12th state machine beyond the 10 this budget books, encroaching on the 2-SM spare margin; not evaluated further because no such concurrent 5th/6th bidirectional-DShot user is named in the specification or in any selection.json part.
combinations.resources: Not computed beyond the observation that only 2 spare state machines remain under the assumed bind order above; a design that needs a genuinely separate PIO consumer beyond the receiver and PPM (for example, a second, non-multiplexed programmer channel) would need to be checked against those 2 spares specifically.
combinations.source: checkout e13f5f60d2e5 hardware/docs/IOBoard.md:258-259; this session's own arithmetic from the state-machine budget above
